questions.question: What is beeswax?
questions.solution_html: What is beeswax? Beeswax is a natural wax produced by honeybees by using their four pairs of wax glands situated on the anterior part of the worker’s last four normal sternal plates. Bees secrete it as a liquid that hardens into scales upon contact with air, and they use these scales to build the hexagonal cells of their honeycomb. It is composed mainly of esters of fatty acids and long-chain alcohols, free fatty acids, hydrocarbons and other minor components (eg. Carotenoids, propolis etc.).
